clue.text: Daughter to behave theatrically, being put down

parts.note: to emote is to act with exaggerated feeling, as on stage

explanation.surface: A daughter who throws tantrums gets snubbed or belittled for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate someone to a lower rank is to put them down in status.

clue.text: Walked with sloppy stride, pace half reduced?

indicators.note: sloppy suggests something done carelessly, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the word pace is cut down to its first half, two of its four letters

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles along with a careless gait, their pace cut by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half reduced' keeps PA from 'pace'; 'sloppy' then rearranges STRIDE plus PA.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, so the past tense is a kind of walking.

clue.text: Beefeaters, perhaps, as men in festival finishing early

indicators.note: the men are placed in the cut-down festival word
the festival word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a carnival is a festive celebration
OR (other ranks) is the crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: Tower of London guards turn out at a festival that wraps up ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' trims the festival's last letter and 'in' sets the men inside. Beefeaters are the Tower of London's ceremonial guards, but here the word is read literally as meat-eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal eaters of beef are meat-eaters, examples of the zoological order of flesh-eating mammals.

clue.text: Dog bringing back one grand, fabulous bird

indicators.note: bringing back tells us to read the string of pieces in the opposite direction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A dog fetches back a thousand pounds and a mythical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing back' turns I G ROC round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh breed of short-legged herding dog, famously kept by the Queen.

clue.text: Mothers bowling American uncle over

indicators.note: bowling someone over knocks them flat, upending them, so the word is turned round
over completes the phrase bowling over, toppling the uncle so his name runs backwards

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: Mums knock over their visiting relative from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal plural for mums, the familiar word for maternal parents.

clue.text: Knowing bishop has hold-up crossing US estuary

indicators.note: the hold-up word stretches across the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a delay is a hold-up
knowing means aware
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A shrewd churchman is held up while crossing an American inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' has the hold-up spanning both the knowing word and the bishop; 'has' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The named inlet where the Delaware River meets the Atlantic, between New Jersey and Delaware.

clue.text: Old TV hospital series that is shown in club

parts.note: M*A*S*H was a long-running US sitcom set in a mobile army hospital
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A classic hospital comedy is screened at a social club.
explanation.definitionFit: An old golf iron with a lofted face, roughly a modern five iron.

clue.text: Once more put out, showing hesitation about having children

indicators.note: about turns the hesitation sound round

parts.note: er is the sound of a hesitation
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates about whether to have kids.
explanation.definitionFit: To publish or release again is to put something out a second time.

clue.text: Pipe of a smoker in church — last thing priest wants

indicators.note: the smoker is set within the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
lum is a Scots word for a chimney, something that smokes

indicators.note: only the final letter of priest is used

explanation.surface: A smoker's pipe in church is the last thing a priest wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the smoker inside the church, and 'last thing' picks priest's final letter. 'Smoker' looks like a person but is a Scots word for a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: The long ornamented tobacco pipe of North American peoples, smoked as a token of peace.

clue.text: Country with no area lacking fertility

indicators.note: with no means the area letter is removed

parts.note: Hungary is a country of central Europe

explanation.surface: A country that has no barren region.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry soil is poor, unproductive land, so the word can describe barrenness.

clue.text: Like a tired kangaroo in forbidden territory?

definitions.meaning: an exhausted kangaroo has no more hops left in it
somewhere one is banned from entering

explanation.definitionFit: A worn-out kangaroo has run out of jumps, while a place off limits lies beyond permitted limits.

clue.text: The old man articulated an expression of disgust

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like this

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: Father voiced his disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection of contempt, like 'bah'.

clue.text: Line taken by ship moving slowly

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A rope is taken aboard a vessel that is sailing at a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning slow and broad.

clue.text: One fixing apparatus is seen around end of kitchen getting higher up

indicators.note: around means the word is surrounds the next piece
only the last letter of kitchen is taken

parts.note: taller means higher

explanation.surface: A fitter working near the far end of a kitchen climbs higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N, from 'end of kitchen', inside IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fits equipment, such as a kitchen fitter, puts it in place.

clue.text: Deviation that's surprising after revolution — disagreement must be restricted

indicators.note: the disagreement is confined within the other letters
after a revolution the exclamation is turned right round

parts.note: egad is an old exclamation of surprise
a rift is a disagreement

explanation.surface: A surprising deviation after a political revolution, where dissent must be curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns the old oath round, and 'must be restricted' confines the disagreement within it. 'That's surprising' stands for an exclamation, not a comment.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount a ship or aircraft is carried off course by currents or wind is its deviation.

clue.text: Person who's very good and competent needed by firm

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a very good person
able means competent

explanation.surface: A firm needs a virtuous and capable employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and steady are synonyms, describing something not easily moved.

clue.text: Leave the City bathed in rank air

indicators.note: the City letters are immersed in the damp

parts.note: damp is a heavy, unwholesome air, as in a mine
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Escape the financial district, soaked in foul air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathed in' immerses the City's postcode in the rank air. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly, often secretly.

clue.text: Various materials produced in plant

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take on a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A range of materials is manufactured in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a botanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A water plant with whorls of narrow leaves round an upright stem.

clue.text: The first person in jazz to generate a sort of chord

indicators.note: the pronoun goes in the jazz word

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A soloist in a jazz band improvises a chord.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-note chord of root, third and fifth.

clue.text: Exceptional horse at Windsor, showing reliability on the track?

indicators.note: exceptional implies something out of the ordinary, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An outstanding racehorse at Windsor shows it can be relied on to run well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the track' suggests a racecourse but means the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitness of a vehicle to be driven safely is dependability on the road.

clue.text: Suffers a tiny bit making attack

parts.note: incurs means suffers or brings upon oneself
an ion is a tiny charged particle

explanation.surface: Someone takes a little damage in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid or invasion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Get rid of stunted growth

definitions.meaning: to cancel or abandon a plan
low bushes and stunted trees covering land

explanation.definitionFit: To cancel something is informal slang; separately, low scrubland vegetation.

clue.text: Farmers mind year being out of kilter

indicators.note: out of kilter means out of order, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Farmers don't care that the year has gone badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who keep cows for milk are a kind of farmer.

clue.text: Boring oldster is young after transformation

indicators.note: a transformation changes form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull old person becomes young again after a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Tediously dull work crushes the spirit, so it is deeply boring.

clue.text: People left behind to support soldiers in van

definitions.text: People left behind to support soldiers

parts.note: being in means being at home
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: Civilians at home stay behind to back the troops in a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The civilian population in wartime, supporting the war effort while troops fight abroad.

clue.text: After end of his journey, driver maybe appears in seedy joint

indicators.note: after puts the journey following the letter from his
just the last letter of his

parts.note: a trip is a journey
a driver is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A cab driver finishes his journey and turns up at a sleazy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist but is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub featuring striptease is a classic disreputable venue.

clue.text: Second child having initially messed about — not loudly — gets disciplined

indicators.note: not means the loudly letter goes

parts.note: fooled about means messed about
F, forte, is the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A second child, having fooled around early on, is quietly disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' marks that the F is lost from the start of FOOLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooled means trained or brought under control, as in schooled horses.

clue.text: Admission fee for child with adult?

definitions.meaning: a child minded by a grown-up is in that adult's care

explanation.definitionFit: A price demanded is one sense; a person in someone's care, like a ward, is another.

clue.text: Is rubbish piled up in trunks?

indicators.note: in a down entry, piled up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Is there junk heaped up in the travel cases?
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' reads the whole string from the bottom of the down entry upwards; 'trunks' suggests luggage but means bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Trunks are human torsos, bodies without head or limbs; the answer is the plural.

clue.text: Barely sufficient examination given minimal time

parts.note: a scan is a close look or medical examination
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An inspection that gets very little time is hardly adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means meagre, only just enough.
